clue.text: Ariadne's oddly selected helper

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered letters of the name Ariadne are chosen, the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A helper picked out by the mythical Ariadne, perhaps to guide Theseus through the labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant or aide-de-camp is a person who helps someone more senior.

clue.text: Athenian clad in some brittle metal

indicators.note: one piece is dressed in, so wrapped by, the other, so the Athenian goes inside the word for some

parts.note: some means any, as in 'have you any?'
Timon of Athens is the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A man of ancient Athens dressed in armour of a fragile metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clad in' means the Athenian is wrapped by the word for some; Timon is Shakespeare's misanthropic Athenian.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a silvery, brittle metalloid element, symbol Sb.

clue.text: Set off from school in time

indicators.note: the school is placed in the word for time, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone sets out from school on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is a link; 'Set off' looks like departing but means exploding.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off, making it explode.

clue.text: One female unknown, introduced to acting, drying up

indicators.note: the three short pieces are inserted into the word for acting

parts.note: mumming is acting in a traditional folk play, as mummers do
I is the Roman numeral for one
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An actress, an unknown, takes to the stage and dries, forgetting her lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drying up' suggests an actor forgetting lines, but it means preserving a body by drying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummifying preserves a body by desiccating it, as the Egyptians did.

clue.text: Given a raise — initially unacceptably poor pay eventually doubled

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A worker got a pay rise only after unacceptably poor pay was finally doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: To up something is to increase it, so a sum that has been upped has been raised.

clue.text: Vegetarian food for omnivore?

parts.note: the name of this pea pod is French for 'eat everything', just what an omnivore does, though the food is a vegetable

explanation.surface: Asking what meat-free dish would suit someone who eats anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The vegetable's French name literally means 'eats all', so its name fits an omnivore while the food itself is vegetarian.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat pea pod, eaten whole, is a vegetarian food whose French name describes an omnivore.

clue.text: Christmas present — open with anger

parts.note: frank means open or candid
to incense is to anger

explanation.surface: Someone tears open a Christmas present angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: FRANK plus INCENSE; 'with' just joins the two. The gift of the Magi is the Christmas present meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankincense was one of the three gifts the Magi brought to the infant Jesus, the first Christmas presents.

clue.text: Absolutely denied being wrong

indicators.note: the letters of the word denied are wrong, so they are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone flatly denies that they were mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an emphatic yes, like certainly or absolutely.

clue.text: It's a nuisance having to go around and take a plane

parts.note: to gad about is to go around looking for pleasure
to fly is to travel by plane

explanation.surface: It's a bother when you must travel about and catch a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: GAD plus FLY; 'and' simply joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadfly is an irritating person who provokes others, a pest.

clue.text: By the sound of it, excessively short skirt

indicators.note: this phrase says that a word is heard rather than read, so its spelling changes

parts.note: too-too is an old phrase meaning excessively or extremely

explanation.surface: A skirt that seems far too short.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt worn by a ballerina.

clue.text: Liberal hoped an end might be made of it

indicators.note: the answer could be formed out of these letters when they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician wished something could be brought to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPEDANEND is rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-handed is generous, giving freely, which is a sense of liberal.

clue.text: One with craft to be PM?

definitions.text: One with craft to be PM?

parts.words: One with craft to be PM?
parts.note: a prime minister makes up a cabinet of ministers; read literally, a craftsman who makes cabinets of furniture

explanation.surface: Asking whether a crafty politician has what it takes to be Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is Prime Minister, who forms the Cabinet; the craft is actually joinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A joiner who builds fine furniture such as cupboards, and in another sense the prime minister who forms a government.

clue.text: Mistreat chap with a title

parts.note: a chap is a man
a handle is slang for a title or name

explanation.surface: Someone abuses a man who holds a title.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN plus HANDLE; 'with a' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle someone is to treat them roughly, pushing them about.

clue.text: Signal death of king and royal mistress

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Nell Gwyn was mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: Announcing the death of a king and of his mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: K plus NELL; 'of' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the tolling of a bell to mark a death; the definition reads it as the bell's sign.

clue.text: Love action, showing no fear

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis
doing means action, as in 'it takes some doing'

explanation.surface: Romantic action taken without any fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No fear!' is British slang for 'certainly not!', which matches the refusal 'nothing doing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal flat refusals, meaning certainly not or no way.

clue.text: Virtuous girl's sincerity

parts.note: virtuous means good
Faith is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A good girl shows sincerity.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in good faith means acting honestly and with sincere intentions.

clue.text: What's for pudding? Is a lemon possibly the answer?

indicators.note: possibly suggests the words that follow can be arranged in another order

explanation.surface: A diner asks what dessert is, and wonders if it might be a lemon.
explanation.walkthrough: ISALEMON rearranged gives the pudding; 'the answer' is a link that pretends to ask a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is a milk pudding made with coarse wheat, a classic school dessert.

clue.text: Strewth! It's no good for women's power

indicators.note: one piece stands for another, so the abbreviation for no good replaces the letter for women

parts.note: strewth is a British exclamation of surprise, here taken as written
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that something is useless for women's power.
explanation.walkthrough: In STREWTH, 'for' puts NG in place of W, giving STRE-NG-TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength is physical power or force.

clue.text: Let the blow be viewed as out of order here

definitions.text: Let the blow be viewed as out of order here

indicators.note: the words are put out of their order and rearranged; out of order also means unfair

explanation.surface: A boxing referee rules a punch to be a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: LETTHEBLOWBE rearranges into the answer, and the whole clue describes an illegal punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch landing beneath the waistband is illegal in boxing, hence any unfair act.

clue.text: Various blood groups found among natives in African forest

definitions.text: found among natives in African forest

parts.note: B, A, O and AB are the blood groups of the ABO system
B, A, O and AB are the blood groups of the ABO system
B, A, O and AB are the blood groups of the ABO system
B, A, O and AB are the blood groups of the ABO system
B, A, O and AB are the blood groups of the ABO system

explanation.surface: Blood samples of several types collected from local people in an African forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Five groups in a row, B, A, O, B and AB, spell the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is a huge tree native to Africa, so it grows there among the native species.

clue.text: Fare from Middle East pupil affluently could afford

indicators.note: afford also means provide or yield, so these words supply the answer from within their letters

explanation.surface: A rich student can afford a Middle Eastern dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'pupIL AFFluently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaff is a rice dish from the Middle East, cooked with spices and stock.

clue.text: American cutter goes to island, it's assumed

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A US cutter heads for an island, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to' joins the pieces. The Isle of Man is an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a proposition taken as self-evident, a starting point that is accepted without proof.

clue.text: Material for making path, of standard weight

parts.note: a standard is a flag
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Asking what material is used to make a path of a given standard weight.
explanation.walkthrough: FLAG plus STONE; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat paving slab used for laying walks and patios.

clue.text: A fellow without right dress

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for fellow surrounds the abbreviation for right

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: A man who has no proper dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': DON goes around R, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn is to decorate, as to dress a window or a room.

clue.text: Murderous female taking champagne on jet

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the champagne follows the jet

parts.note: jet black is a deep black
the Widow is a nickname for Veuve Clicquot champagne, veuve being French for widow

explanation.surface: A woman who kills, sipping champagne aboard a jet.
explanation.walkthrough: Veuve Clicquot is a champagne house; its nickname 'the Widow' gives WIDOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The black widow spider is noted for the female sometimes eating the male after mating.

clue.text: Call round

definitions.meaning: to telephone someone is to give them a call
a circle or band is a round shape

explanation.definitionFit: To ring is to telephone, and a ring is a circular band, something round.

clue.text: Leaders of brave enemy shot in advance

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their opening letters

parts.note: a forehand is a shot in tennis

explanation.surface: Heads of a brave enemy force shot before it advanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Beforehand means earlier, ahead of time.

clue.text: Blight has finally killed tree

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word killed

parts.note: an ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A disease that killed off a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: D plus ASH; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash hopes is to ruin or blight them.
